title: Inktoll: AI reads your work, Inktoll makes it pay

lines.text: How do stablecoin payment rails actually settle?
Four seconds. That is how long the answer took. To write it, the model read work by a human who will never know, never be credited, and never be paid.
This is the biggest unpaid tab on the internet. Agents read everything. Writers earn nothing.
So publishers build walls. Paywalls, blocks, robots dot txt. The open web fractures, and the writers still do not get paid.
But a wall is not a price. There has never been a way for a machine to simply pay a writer two cents and move on.
A writer connects a wallet and publishes through Paragraph. Authorship is checked against that wallet, so nobody can paste someone else's link and take the money.
An agent finds the article and meets an HTTP four oh two. Payment required. It signs a USDC authorization, and the text comes back.
When that knowledge becomes an answer, the writer is paid again. A citation toll, every single time.
Every payment leaves a public receipt, settled on Arc.
Two things make this possible. Gas is paid in USDC, so a two cent toll is not absurd. And Circle Gateway batches the signatures, so a thousand reads are not a thousand transactions.
An MCP server lets any AI assistant pay for what it reads, without knowing what a blockchain is.
Inktoll. Readers pay once. Creators earn forever.
